title: Allow disabling unused dissectors from PHS dialog
description:
Implements the feature request in #16923.

UI changes:

Adds two major new features to the Protocol Hierarchy Statistics (PHS)
GUI.  One disables all dissectors, then re-enables only the dissectors
shown in the dialog (and thus, only for the protocols used in the
current file).  The other feature reverts this change if possible (see
notes below).

Adds `Copy > protocol short names` to the PHS GUI. Copies the list of
protocol short names in use to the clipboard, comma-separated, for use
on the command line.

Command line `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` (and
`--enable-heuristic/--disable-heuristic`) options now accept
multiple protocol names separated by commas, to allow en/disabling
multiple protocols at once with less typing.

Command line `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` options now accept
'ALL' as an argument. For `--disable-protocol`, disables all protocols.
For `--enable-protocol`, enables all protocols *that are not disabled by
default.*

API changes:

`proto_enable_proto_by_name()` now always enables protocols that it is
asked to enable. Old behaviour was to only enable protocols that are
disabled by default. This behaviour change allows the new "disable
unused protocols" feature in the PHS GUI to function as it's described
above. This also allows command-line options such as `tshark
--disable-protocol ALL --enable-protocol eth,ip` to provide equivalent
functionality as the new GUI feature.

Added `proto_disable_heuristic_by_name()` which takes a protocol name as
its single argument. Revised `proto_enable_heuristic_by_name()` to also
only take a single argument. This was changed to simplify the use of
both functions as callbacks in `ui/dissect_opts.c` (which is where
was added support for comma-separated protocol names).

`proto_enable_proto_by_name()` and `proto_disable_proto_by_name()` now
return a boolean, true if the requested protocol exists and false if
not, for API symmetry with `proto_enable_heuristic_by_name()`.

Track when changes made to the enabled/disabled status of protocols
have not yet been saved to the user's profile, and make this information
available via a new function `enabled_protos_unsaved_changes()` in
`epan/disabled_protos.c`. This could already occur when using
`--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` for Wireshark; now it is also
possible if the new "disable unused protocols" feature on the PHS GUI is
used.

Made `read_enabled_and_disabled_lists()` in `epan/disabled_protos.h`
a public function, as this seemed the most minimal way to undo changes
to the enabled/disabled status of protocols. The suggested alternative
of calling `epan_load_settings()` would also revert other unsaved
changes, particularly to user preferences. If that behaviour is
preferred over exposing this function, then it can be done.

Notes:

As has always been the case, if one uses
`--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` on the Wireshark command line,
then goes to `Analyze > Enabled Protocols...` and makes changes,
these changes cause the enabled/disabled state of all protocols to
be written to the user's profile. This is more important to note now
that large numbers of protocols can be easily enabled/disabled
from the command line.

The temporary changes made by the new PHS GUI feature are also subject
to this behaviour. As a result, if one makes changes in the Enabled
Protocols dialog, it becomes impossible to return all protocols to the
enabled/disabled state they had before making use of the new feature.

Other:

It may make sense for `--enable-protocol ALL` to enable all protocols
*including* those which are disabled by default. The function
`proto_reenable_all()` in `epan/proto.c` would need to be modified or
duplicated in order to allow this behaviour.

It may make sense for the button which resets protocol enabled/disabled
status to appear on the Enabled Protocols dialog. I investigated this,
but lack sufficient Qt knowledge to cause this reset to be reflected in
the state of the checkboxes in the dialog.

Closes #16923

notes.body:
I have a few issues here. I don't see an issue with copying the protocol names, just to have that functionality a little bit different, as that specific menu is meant as something else. But at the moment, I cannot see a better place as well. One could add it to the context menu, but there the reasoning is often, that only functions that are available someplace else should be put into context menus.

I have a bigger issue with the disable/enable functionality. We already have a similar functionality in the "Enabled protocols" dialog. There you can enable/disable or invert. I am not really sure what "Revert" should achieve. Let's assume you have a bunch of protocols disabled, then open this dialog and disable the protocols. If you revert will you get all the protocols back or will the already disabled protocols stay? If you close the dialog you cannot revert at all?

I would much rather see this functionality in the same terms as "Enabled protocols" and be able to enable/disable.

Overall, could it not make more sense, to add an additional filter to "Enabled protocols", to only show protocols present in the file? You would get the same result, just with a lot fewer changes and also the functionality for mass-enable/disable would stay in the same dialog, instead of adding functionality someplace else.

> Overall, could it not make more sense, to add an additional filter to "Enabled protocols", to only show protocols present in the file? You would get the same result, just with a lot fewer changes and also the functionality for mass-enable/disable would stay in the same dialog, instead of adding functionality someplace else.

I do not believe that this approach would result in fewer changes. In fact, I think it could lead to *more* changes. It was relatively trivial for me to add the feature to the PHS dialog, because this dialog is already collecting the list of protocols in use in the file; I got the protocol short names almost "for free." For the Enabled Protocols dialog to have this same feature, it would need to do its own scan over the entire file to find what protocols are in use.

Note that I'm not discouraging this idea, just managing expectations about what it would entail.

> I would much rather see this functionality in the same terms as "Enabled protocols" and be able to enable/disable.

It would make more sense from an end-user standpoint for the feature to be in the Enabled Protocols dialog. Assuming the feature would get a new button on this dialog, then we could wait to scan the file for its protocols until the button is actually pressed. The scan would still take a long time on large files, but at least it wouldn't impact the dialog's initial load time.

> I am not really sure what "Revert" should achieve. Let's assume you have a bunch of protocols disabled, then open this dialog and disable the protocols. If you revert will you get all the protocols back or will the already disabled protocols stay? If you close the dialog you cannot revert at all?

To make discussion easier, I will define "temporary changes" to the enabled/disabled state of protocols: these are changes that exist in Wireshark's memory and affect its dissection, but which have not been saved to the user's profile. They are lost when Wireshark exits.

When you say "open this dialog and disable the protocols" I assume you mean the PHS dialog. As written in this patch, these changes are temporary. If you use the revert function it will revert those specific changes (and also protocols that were disabled with `--disable-protocol` on the Wireshark command line; see below) but it will leave protocols disabled that you disabled in the Enabled Protocols dialog.

Note that any change made on the Enabled Protocols dialog causes *all* enabled/disabled protocols to be written to the user's profile -- that is to say, "temporary" changes cease to be temporary. This dialog does not currently have a way to make temporary changes. If we're fortunate, then it may be straightforward to add a "Save" button to this dialog, and have all changes made in this dialog be temporary unless/until one clicks Save. (This would parallel the behaviour of the Decode As dialog, for example.) If we're less fortunate then it will take more work.

The concept of temporarily enabling/disabling protocols in Wireshark seems to be incompletely thought out. Apart from this patch, the only way it's used is in the `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` command line options to Wireshark. That alone may be a good reason to reject this patch, because it makes use of a "feature" which may not be intentional.

I do think it's a useful feature to have, though. I will investigate adding a Save button to the Enabled Protocols dialog.

> I do not believe that this approach would result in fewer changes. In fact, I think it could lead to *more* changes. It was relatively trivial for me to add the feature to the PHS dialog, because this dialog is already collecting the list of protocols in use in the file; I got the protocol short names almost "for free." For the Enabled Protocols dialog to have this same feature, it would need to do its own scan over the entire file to find what protocols are in use.

No it doesn't. It is actually much less. You would just need to add the same tap as it is being used for the protocol hierarchy. Therefore, it is actually much less code and would require next to none changes to the underlying epan ecosystem.

That's another thing. Enabling/Disabling a bunch of dissectors is already implemented and can easily be adapted to be used in the fashion you require. Implementing new methods just seems to be counterintuitive.

> It would make more sense from an end-user standpoint for the feature to be in the Enabled Protocols dialog. Assuming the feature would get a new button on this dialog, then we could wait to scan the file for its protocols until the button is actually pressed. The scan would still take a long time on large files, but at least it wouldn't impact the dialog's initial load time.

Again, no need for waiting, same loading time as for the hierarchy dialog.

> To make discussion easier, I will define "temporary changes" to the enabled/disabled state of protocols: these are changes that exist in Wireshark's memory and affect its dissection, but which have not been saved to the user's profile. They are lost when Wireshark exits.
> 
> When you say "open this dialog and disable the protocols" I assume you mean the PHS dialog. As written in this patch, these changes are temporary. If you use the revert function it will revert those specific changes (and also protocols that were disabled with `--disable-protocol` on the Wireshark command line; see below) but it will leave protocols disabled that you disabled in the Enabled Protocols dialog.
> 
> Note that any change made on the Enabled Protocols dialog causes *all* enabled/disabled protocols to be written to the user's profile -- that is to say, "temporary" changes cease to be temporary. This dialog does not currently have a way to make temporary changes. If we're fortunate, then it may be straightforward to add a "Save" button to this dialog, and have all changes made in this dialog be temporary unless/until one clicks Save. (This would parallel the behaviour of the Decode As dialog, for example.) If we're less fortunate then it will take more work.
> 
> The concept of temporarily enabling/disabling protocols in Wireshark seems to be incompletely thought out. Apart from this patch, the only way it's used is in the `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` command line options to Wireshark. That alone may be a good reason to reject this patch, because it makes use of a "feature" which may not be intentional.
> 
> I do think it's a useful feature to have, though. I will investigate adding a Save button to the Enabled Protocols dialog.

This actually breaks a lot of usability Wireshark currently has. 

To clarify in that regard. If you change configuration, it should neither be temporary, nor require special handling to be saved. It should be repeatable and predictive. Both is not always the case here. e.g. you can disable a bunch of protocols but reenabling will enable not all disabled ones, as they have been disabled by another method?

Also, please don't implement a separate save button. Profiles are not "temporary", and I can easily see people destroying their profiles, because they accidentally enabled/disabled some protocols. 

To be clear, my issue here is predictability and repeatability. The same method if reversed should lead to the same outcome. A -> B  =  B -> A. In this case here it is more likely to be A -> B = B -> A'.

I accept the idea and think it can be useful. And as such it would be a nice feature to add. But I would much rather see the functionality to be channelized within the "Enabled Protocols" dialog (as the name suggests, that's where the functionality will be searched for), than the Hierarchy dialog.

You seem to have misunderstood at least some of my comment. I'm not against the idea of adding the feature to the Enabled Protocols dialog at all. I actually said it would make more sense to the user if it were there. I'm sorry that I wasn't clear that I'm agreeing with you; hopefully it is clearer now.

Could you please quote smaller sections of my comments so I can better understand the concerns you're having?

> To clarify in that regard. If you change configuration, it should neither be temporary, nor require special handling to be saved.

You should know that this is the behaviour that you get with the "Decode As" functionality, as I said above. It has separate buttons for "OK" and "Save". Only "Save" causes the change to be written to the user's profile. Clicking "OK" *without* clicking "Save" causes one's changes to apply only for the remainder of the current Wireshark session.

To put it another way, the "Decode As" changes are *temporary* until the user explicitly makes them permanent.

I believe this is also the behaviour you get if you right-click in a packet's protocol tree and change one of its settings that way. Changes made there do not persist beyond the current Wireshark session, unless you go to the Preferences dialog and also make changes there. Saving your preferences from this dialog causes all preference changes to be saved and no longer temporary.

That is the precedent I was using to inspire my suggestion of a similar Save button on the Enabled Protocols dialog. It would allow the user to temporarily enable or disable protocols without "destroying their profiles, because they accidentally enabled/disabled some protocols" as you put it.

By the way, this is a risk that exists right now -- without my patch -- and which we have no way of mitigating. Check out master, build it, run it, and imagine you've disabled some protocols previously in your profile. If you go to Enabled Protocols, click Disable All, and click OK, then I hope you backed up your profile, because that's the only way you can get back to the set of disabled protocols that you had before making this mistake.

To clarify, my idea of adding a Save button to the Enabled Protocols dialog is meant to be *entirely independent of this patch*. I think it would mesh nicely with solving the problem that this patch also aims to solve, but I also think it would be a helpful feature on its own.

> Profiles are not "temporary",

I never said they were. In fact, I was explicit in defining that the state of being "temporary" *ended* when the changes were written to the profile on disk. I evidently did a poor job of explaining this, for which I apologize.

> To be clear, my issue here is predictability and repeatability. The same method if reversed should lead to the same outcome. A -> B = B -> A. In this case here it is more likely to be A -> B = B -> A'.

I guess I again have failed to make myself clear. This patch, as currently written, **does** give the behaviour `A -> B = B -> A`. It only breaks this rule if you do something in the Enabled Protocols dialog, thus adding a `C` state.

But again, I'm not married to this specific implementation. As I hope I've made clear by now, I like the idea of having this feature in the Enabled Protocols dialog instead.

> No it doesn't. It is actually much less. You would just need to add the same tap as it is being used for the protocol hierarchy. Therefore, it is actually much less code and would require next to none changes to the underlying epan ecosystem.

Perhaps it seems like it would be more code to me because I am not a Qt expert like you. I did look at adding this feature to the Enabled Protocols dialog (as you'll see in my commit message / review summary message), but I could not get the checkboxes to reflect changes in a protocol's enabled/disabled status that were made by routines in that dialog.

The epan changes are still necessary if we want to have an equivalent feature for TShark, which I do.

> That's another thing. Enabling/Disabling a bunch of dissectors is already implemented and can easily be adapted to be used in the fashion you require. Implementing new methods just seems to be counterintuitive.

I'm confused. I only implemented one new method, `proto_disable_all()`. I call that, and then call `proto_enable_proto_by_name()` on the protocols that exist in this file. How is this counterintuitive? What would you suggest instead that would make more sense? Keep in mind that I also want equivalent functionality in TShark.

I genuinely want to learn how to be a better contributor. And it seems like you already have a strong idea of how this could be done. Would you be interested in doing your own approach for addressing #16923? If you do, please tag me on your pull request, so I can see what you mean.

commits_data.message:
Allow disabling unused dissectors from PHS dialog

Implements the feature request in #16923.

UI changes:

Adds two major new features to the Protocol Hierarchy Statistics (PHS)
GUI.  One disables all dissectors, then re-enables only the dissectors
shown in the dialog (and thus, only for the protocols used in the
current file).  The other feature reverts this change if possible (see
notes below).

Adds `Copy > protocol short names` to the PHS GUI. Copies the list of
protocol short names in use to the clipboard, comma-separated, for use
on the command line.

Command line `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` (and
`--enable-heuristic/--disable-heuristic`) options now accept
multiple protocol names separated by commas, to allow en/disabling
multiple protocols at once with less typing.

Command line `--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` options now accept
'ALL' as an argument. For `--disable-protocol`, disables all protocols.
For `--enable-protocol`, enables all protocols *that are not disabled by
default.*

API changes:

`proto_enable_proto_by_name()` now always enables protocols that it is
asked to enable. Old behaviour was to only enable protocols that are
disabled by default. This behaviour change allows the new "disable
unused protocols" feature in the PHS GUI to function as it's described
above. This also allows command-line options such as `tshark
--disable-protocol ALL --enable-protocol eth,ip` to provide equivalent
functionality as the new GUI feature.

Added `proto_disable_heuristic_by_name()` which takes a protocol name as
its single argument. Revised `proto_enable_heuristic_by_name()` to also
only take a single argument. This was changed to simplify the use of
both functions as callbacks in `ui/dissect_opts.c` (which is where
was added support for comma-separated protocol names).

`proto_enable_proto_by_name()` and `proto_disable_proto_by_name()` now
return a boolean, true if the requested protocol exists and false if
not, for API symmetry with `proto_enable_heuristic_by_name()`.

Track when changes made to the enabled/disabled status of protocols
have not yet been saved to the user's profile, and make this information
available via a new function `enabled_protos_unsaved_changes()` in
`epan/disabled_protos.c`. This could already occur when using
`--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` for Wireshark; now it is also
possible if the new "disable unused protocols" feature on the PHS GUI is
used.

Made `read_enabled_and_disabled_lists()` in `epan/disabled_protos.h`
a public function, as this seemed the most minimal way to undo changes
to the enabled/disabled status of protocols. The suggested alternative
of calling `epan_load_settings()` would also revert other unsaved
changes, particularly to user preferences. If that behaviour is
preferred over exposing this function, then it can be done.

Notes:

As has always been the case, if one uses
`--enable-protocol/--disable-protocol` on the Wireshark command line,
then goes to `Analyze > Enabled Protocols...` and makes changes,
these changes cause the enabled/disabled state of all protocols to
be written to the user's profile. This is more important to note now
that large numbers of protocols can be easily enabled/disabled
from the command line.

The temporary changes made by the new PHS GUI feature are also subject
to this behaviour. As a result, if one makes changes in the Enabled
Protocols dialog, it becomes impossible to return all protocols to the
enabled/disabled state they had before making use of the new feature.
